<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Sylow23" /></noinclude><section begin="par125" />are made determinate by the article, when they are joined like adjectives (see {{GHGpar|126|u}}) with a determinate substantive, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הָאִישׁ הַזֶּה|translate=this man}}; {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאֲנָשִׁים הָאֵ֫לֶּה|translate=these men}}; {{GHGheb|text=בַּיָּמִים הָהֵ֫מָּה וּבָעֵת הַהִיא|translate=in those days, and in that time}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=4|verse=1}}. The demonstrative, however, even in this case, is frequently used ''without'' the article, as being sufficiently determinate in itself (cf. {{GHGpar|126|y}}).
<section end="par125" />
<section begin="par126" />{{GHGpar-heading|126|Determination by Means of the Article}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|a}}
'''1.''' The article ({{GHGheb|text=הַ·}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֶ}}, § 35) was originally, as in other languages (clearly in the Romance; cf. also ὁ, ἡ, τό in Homer), a demonstrative pronoun. The demonstrative force of the article, apart from its occasional use as a relative pronoun (see {{GHGpar|138|i}}), appears now, however, only (''a'') in a few standing phrases, and (''b'') in a certain class of statements or exclamations.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|b}}
(''a'') Cf. {{GHGheb|text=הַיּוֹם|translate=this day, hodie}} ({{GHGpar|100|c}}); {{GHGheb|text=הַלַּ֫יְלָה|translate=this night}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=34}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַפַּ֫עַם|translate=this time}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=23}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַשָּׁנָה|translate=this year}} (= in this year) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=28|verse=16}}.

(''b'') includes those instances in which the article, mostly when prefixed to a participle, joins on a new statement concerning a preceding noun. Although such participles, &c., are no doubt primarily regarded always as in apposition to a preceding substantive, the article nevertheless has in some of these examples almost the force of {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} ({{GHGheb|text=הִיא}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}}) as the subject of a noun-clause; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=19|verse=10}} ''the judgements of the Lord are true''..., verse 11 {{GHGheb|text=הַנֶּֽחֱמָדִים וג׳}} prop. ''the more to be desired than gold'', i.e. ''they are more to be desired'', or ''even they, that are more to be desired'',<ref>On the analogous use of the article before participles which have a verbal suffix, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=33}}, &c., cf. above, {{GHGpar|116|f}}.</ref> &c.; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=22}} f., 44:27 f., 46:6, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=2|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=33|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=49|verse=7|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=הַבֹּֽטְחִים}} in the parallel half of the verse continued by a finite verb); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=28|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=41|verse=25|hidebook=1}} and frequently. When such a participle has another co-ordinate with it, the latter is used ''without'' the article, since according to the above it strictly speaking represents a second predicate, and as such, according to ''i'', remains indeterminate; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=10}} ''who giveth'' ({{GHGheb|text=הַנֹּתֵן}}) ''rain'', &c., ''and sendeth'' ({{GHGheb|text=וְשֹׁלֵחַ}}), &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|c}}
The article is sometimes used with similar emphasis before a substantive, which serves as the subject of a compound sentence ({{GHGpar|140|d}}); e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=הַצּוּר תָּמִים פָּֽעֳלוֹ}} i.e. as a fresh statement (not in apposition to the preceding dative), really equivalent to ''he is a rock, perfect in his work'' (i.e. ''whose work is perfect''); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=31}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|d}}
'''2.''' The article is, generally speaking, employed to determine a substantive wherever it is required by Greek and English; thus:

(''a'') When a person or thing already spoken of is mentioned again, and is consequently more definite to the mind of the hearer or reader; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=3}} ''and God said, Let there be light'': verse 4 ''and God saw the light'' ({{GHGheb|text=אֶת־הָאוֹר}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=3|verse=24}} ''fetch me a sword: and they brought the sword''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=9|verse=15}}. (In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=2}} therefore {{GHGheb|text=לֶֽעָשִׁיר}} must be read.)<section end="par126" /><noinclude>
